title: T1071.001 — Application Layer Protocol - Web Protocols
subtitle: Press play to watch an implant on FIN-WS-04 talk to a compromised blog through the corporate proxy.
aria: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol - Web Protocols

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Delivery
steps.caption: An employee opens invoice.docm on FIN-WS-04. A macro runs a small loader (a tiny program that downloads the real malware). The loader makes its first web call through the corporate proxy. the proxy logs winword.exe as the client process, and cdn-updates[.]com appears for the first time on the estate
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Check-in
steps.caption: The loader POSTs host details to /wp-content/uploads/gate.php. It hides the data in a cookie value encoded with base64 (a text encoding that turns any data into letters and digits). The C2 answers with a task inside a Set-Cookie header. a POST of exactly 1042 bytes to a blog URL, with a large Set-Cookie response, deserves a second look
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The 60-second metronome
steps.caption: The implant beacons every 60 seconds plus or minus 3 seconds of jitter (small random changes in timing). Every POST body is 1042 bytes. 18 regular beacons with a size spread below 1 percent. Humans browse at random, so timing this clean is a machine
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Masquerade
steps.caption: The beacon claims to be Internet Explorer 7 and shifts some traffic to quiet hours to look like legacy web use. the user-agent (UA - the browser name string a client sends with each request) does not match the Windows 11 operating system. The JA3 hash (a fingerprint of the client's TLS handshake) also does not look like a real browser
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Task: harvest and send
steps.caption: The implant collects saved browser passwords. It splits them into eight POST bodies and uploads about 4.1 MB in total. egress bytes per process rise, and the uploads go to a domain that is only 21 days old
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: C2 rotation
steps.caption: DNS for cdn-updates[.]com now returns 198.51.100.77 instead of 198.51.100.23. The beacon follows the new address without any change on the host. the destination IP changed mid-session while the SNI (the domain name a client names during the TLS handshake) and the URL path stayed the same. Watch the domain, not one IP
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Proxy alert fires
steps.caption: The SIEM (the central system that collects logs and raises alerts) joins the legacy user-agent with the 60-second periodicity. Rule BEACON-01 fires for FIN-WS-04. pull 24 hours of proxy logs for the host, then check domain age and reputation before you escalate
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Contain
steps.caption: The proxy denies cdn-updates[.]com. The host is isolated from the network. A 30-day retro hunt (a search through stored old logs) finds no other host with the same pattern. block the domain first, because the IP rotates. Preserve logs, then reimage the host
